title: The Concept of Social Stratification
text:
Social stratification refers to a society's categorization of its people into rankings based on factors such as wealth, income, race, and educational qualifications. This hierarchical structure determines unequal access to resources and opportunities across different groups.

Societies employ various systems—such as class systems, caste systems, or status groups—to maintain these rigid boundaries. These mechanisms dictate mobility and often reproduce inequality across generations, forming foundational structures of social reality.

The examination of stratification helps scholars understand how power is distributed unevenly. It suggests that systemic disparities are not merely accidental but are built into the operational framework of societal organization.
